B.best_element: Offers a user-owned Google Apps Script web app ('execute as me', addPopupReminder) as an alternative calendar route. It avoids the GCP OAuth client setup, the 7-day Testing refresh-token expiry and Google's rejection of Firefox redirect URLs.
B.biggest_weakness: Calls SGW's ToS 'unverified' even though the 2025 ToU explicitly bans extensions and automation, and states unflagged platform claims as fact (Chrome 148 native browser.*, polyfill archived, Google 'needs' the loopback redirect).

C.best_element: Test-only hooks must be compiled out of production with a CI check that proves it, alongside a threat-model table that names the test proving each control and a manifest-permission snapshot that fails on any new permission.
C.biggest_weakness: Leaves the SGW ToS stance as 'unknown' (the ToU explicitly prohibits it). Prior art is thin and there is no Google personal-use or verification path. 'Firefox host permissions are opt-in' is outdated: Firefox 127+ grants them at install.

D.best_element: A Site Adapter layer (DOM/API/Session/Clock) with versioned selector and endpoint config and a healthCheck() that automatically disables all write automation on drift. Downstream tasks consume only recon-spike fixtures.
D.biggest_weakness: Google Calendar auth is nearly absent despite unattended daily writes: no refresh-token strategy, no 7-day Testing expiry, no Firefox redirect plan. It also asks for Playwright e2e that loads the extension in Firefox, which Playwright doesn't support.

E.best_element: The insight that favoriting may attract bidders, answered with a per-watch auto-favorite choice and a 'local-only watch' alternative. Also the rule that hiding is never silent: a per-card 'Why?' plus one-click undo.
E.biggest_weakness: Heavy UX mandates plus unflagged or contradictory facts: favorite notes ≤500 (the source code says 256), 'no clock extension' and the 15-auction cap stated as fact. Calendar auth is thin, so the plan risks being wide rather than cleanly decomposed.

F.best_element: A mock buyerapi with injectable latency, clock skew, error codes, token expiry and soft-close extension, plus a rule that any real-money test needs explicit user approval for a specific cheap item.
F.biggest_weakness: Over-invests in the nice-to-have snipe engine. Requirements 1–4 get a line or two each (highlight/hide, daily check, calendar auth with no refresh-token or expiry handling), and it also assumes Playwright extension e2e on Firefox.

rationale: C beat D because its ports-and-adapters contracts, tests-first task cards with gate commands, CI-proven removal of test hooks, and threat controls mapped to proving tests are the most likely to yield a plan the orchestrator can run in parallel and verify mechanically. D has the strongest site recon and the best drift-gating adapter. But its Google Calendar auth is almost missing (no refresh tokens, no 7-day Testing expiry, no Firefox redirect strategy), and it wrongly assumes Playwright can load Firefox extensions. Neither spells out the personal-use OAuth path.
